title_en: Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China

September 11, 1985      Fa (Min) Fa [1985] No. 22

The Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, adopted at the Third Session of the Sixth National People's Congress, is the guideline for Chinese citizens to handle inheritance issues and the basis for the people's courts to correctly and timely adjudicate inheritance cases. In implementing the Inheritance Law, the people's courts shall adhere to the principles of socialist legal system, uphold equality between men and women in inheritance rights, implement the spirit of mutual assistance and consistency of rights and obligations, and protect citizens' inheritance rights of private property according to law.

In order to correctly implement the Inheritance Law, we propose the following opinions on certain issues concerning the specific application of the Inheritance Law in the adjudication of inheritance cases, based on the relevant provisions of the Inheritance Law and trial practice experience, for the people's courts at all levels to try out when adjudicating inheritance cases.

I. General Provisions

1. Inheritance begins at the time of the decedent's physiological death or declaration of death.

If a missing person is declared dead, the date of death of the missing person determined in the court judgment shall be the time when inheritance begins.

2. If several persons who are entitled to inherit from each other die in the same event and the order of death cannot be determined, it is presumed that the person without heirs dies first. If each of the deceased persons has heirs, and the deceased persons are of different generations, it is presumed that the elder dies first; if the deceased persons are of the same generation, it is presumed that they die simultaneously, and no inheritance occurs between them, and their respective heirs shall inherit separately.

3. Other lawful property that citizens may inherit includes securities and claims for which the subject matter of performance is property.

4. If a contractor dies before receiving the benefits of the contract, the funds invested by the decedent in the contract, the labor expended, and the appreciation and fruits thereof may be reasonably valued and compensated by the party awarding the contract or the person who continues the contract, and the value shall be treated as part of the estate.

5. If a decedent, during his or her lifetime, has entered into a legacy-support agreement with another person and also made a will, after inheritance begins, if there is no conflict between the legacy-support agreement and the will, the estate shall be dealt with separately according to the agreement and the will; if there is a conflict, the estate shall be dealt with according to the agreement, and the part of the will that conflicts with the agreement shall be wholly or partially invalid.

6. After a testamentary heir inherits property under the will, he or she still has the right to inherit the property not disposed of by the will in accordance with Article 13 of the Inheritance Law.

7. Children under six years of age and persons with mental illness may be deemed persons without capacity for civil conduct.

Minors who have reached the age of six but are under the age of eighteen shall be deemed persons with limited capacity for civil conduct.

8. A legal representative, when acting on behalf of the principal to exercise the right of inheritance or the right to accept a legacy, shall not harm the interests of the principal. Generally, a legal representative may not act on behalf of the principal to renounce the right of inheritance or the right to accept a legacy. If the agency act obviously harms the interests of the principal, it shall be deemed invalid.

9. In the inheritance of an estate, if a dispute arises between heirs as to whether the right of inheritance is forfeited and an action is brought to the people's court, the people's court shall, in accordance with Article 7 of the Inheritance Law, determine by judgment whether the right of inheritance is forfeited.

10. Whether an heir's maltreatment of the decedent is serious may be determined based on the time, means, consequences, and social impact of the maltreatment.

If the heir's maltreatment of the decedent is serious, regardless of whether criminal liability is pursued, it may be confirmed that the heir has forfeited the right of inheritance.

11. If an heir intentionally kills the decedent, whether the killing is completed or attempted, it shall be confirmed that the heir has forfeited the right of inheritance.

12. If an heir has committed any of the acts listed in Article 7, items (1) or (2) of the Inheritance Law, and the decedent, by will, designates that the heir shall inherit the estate, the will may be declared invalid, and the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 7 of the Inheritance Law.

13. If an heir seriously maltreats or abandons the decedent, but later shows genuine repentance, and the maltreated or abandoned decedent, during his or her lifetime, expressed forgiveness, the forfeiture of the right of inheritance may not be confirmed.

14. If an heir forges, alters, or destroys a will, thereby infringing upon the interests of an heir who lacks the ability to work and has no source of income, and causes such heir to live in difficulty, the act shall be deemed to be of a serious nature.

15. During the limitation period, if an heir is unable to exercise the right of inheritance due to irresistible causes, the people's court may treat the limitation period as suspended.

16. Within two years from the date the heir becomes aware of the infringement of his or her rights, if the dispute over the inheritance right is indeed being mediated by the People's Mediation Committee, the limitation period may be treated as suspended.

17. If an heir brings a lawsuit to the people's court due to a dispute over inheritance, the limitation period is interrupted.

18. If an heir becomes aware of the infringement of his or her rights only during the period between the eighteenth and the twentieth year after the commencement of inheritance, the right to bring a lawsuit shall be exercised within twenty years from the commencement of inheritance. After twenty years, no lawsuit may be brought.

II. Statutory Inheritance

19. If an adopted child has fulfilled the duty of support towards the adoptive parents and has also provided considerable support to the biological parents, in addition to inheriting the estate of the adoptive parents in accordance with Article 10 of the Inheritance Law, the adopted child may also receive an appropriate share of the estate of the biological parents in accordance with Article 14 of the Inheritance Law.

20. In a polygamous family formed in the old society, if a relationship of support has been formed between the children and other spouses of the father other than the biological mother, they have mutual inheritance rights.

21. The inheritance by a stepchild of the estate of the stepparents does not affect the inheritance by the stepchild of the estate of the biological parents.

The inheritance by a stepparent of the estate of a stepchild does not affect the inheritance by the stepparent of the estate of the biological child.

22. If a person adopts another as a grandchild, and the relationship is treated as that between adoptive parents and adopted children, they may be mutual first-order statutory heirs.

23. Between adopted children and biological children, and between adopted children, if they are considered adoptive siblings, they may be mutual second-order statutory heirs.

The rights and obligations between an adopted person and his or her biological siblings are extinguished upon the establishment of the adoption relationship, and they may not be mutual second-order statutory heirs.

24. The inheritance right between step-siblings arises from the existence of a support relationship between them. If there is no support relationship, they may not be mutual second-order statutory heirs.

If step-siblings have mutually inherited each other's estate, this does not affect their inheritance of the estate of their biological siblings.

25. The grandchildren, maternal grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and great-maternal grandchildren of the decedent may all inherit by subrogation, and there is no limitation on the number of generations for subrogation heirs.

26. The biological children of the decedent's adopted children and stepchildren with whom a support relationship has been formed may inherit by subrogation; the adopted children of the decedent's biological children may inherit by subrogation; the adopted children of the decedent's adopted children may inherit by subrogation; and the adopted children of stepchildren with whom a support relationship has been formed with the decedent may also inherit by subrogation.

27. If a subrogation heir lacks the ability to work and has no source of income, or has performed the primary duty of support towards the decedent, such heir may receive a larger share when the estate is distributed.

28. If an heir forfeits the right of inheritance, his or her lineal descendants may not inherit by subrogation. However, if such subrogation heir lacks the ability to work and has no source of income, or has provided considerable support to the decedent, an appropriate share of the estate may be given.

29. A widowed daughter-in-law who has supported her parents-in-law, or a widowed son-in-law who has supported his parents-in-law, regardless of whether they have remarried, may, as a first-order statutory heir in accordance with Article 12 of the Inheritance Law, and this does not affect the subrogation inheritance of their children.

30. If a person has provided the main financial support for the decedent's living or has given main assistance in terms of labor or other aspects, such person shall be deemed to have fulfilled the primary duty of support or primary duty of maintenance.

31. For a person who may be given an appropriate share of the estate in accordance with Article 14 of the Inheritance Law, when distributing the estate to such person, the share may be more or less than that of an heir, depending on the specific circumstances.

32. A person who may be given an appropriate share of the estate in accordance with Article 14 of the Inheritance Law, if his or her right to lawfully obtain the decedent's estate is infringed, has the right to bring a lawsuit to the people's court as an independent litigant. However, if such person knew of the distribution of the estate but did not make a claim, the lawsuit shall generally not be accepted; if such person did not know and did not make a claim, but brings a lawsuit within two years, the lawsuit shall be accepted.

33. If an heir has the ability and conditions to provide support and is willing to fulfill the support obligation, but the decedent, having a fixed income and the ability to work, explicitly states that he or she does not require support, when distributing the estate, this generally shall not affect the heir's share of inheritance.

34. If an heir who has the ability and conditions to provide support lives together with the decedent but fails to fulfill the support obligation towards the decedent who needs support, when distributing the estate, the heir may receive a smaller share or no share.

III. Testamentary Succession

35. For wills made before the implementation of the Inheritance Law that have slight formal defects, if the content is lawful and there is sufficient evidence to prove that the will truly reflects the testator's intent, the will may be deemed valid.

36. Creditors and debtors of an heir or legatee, and co-partners in a joint business, shall also be regarded as having an interest in the heir or legatee and may not act as witnesses to a will.

37. If a testator fails to reserve a share of the estate for an heir who lacks the ability to work and has no source of income, when the estate is disposed of, a necessary share shall be reserved for such heir, and only the remaining portion may be dealt with by reference to the distribution principles determined in the will.

Whether an heir lacks the ability to work and has no source of income shall be determined based on the specific circumstances of such heir at the time the will takes effect.

38. If a testator, by will, disposes of property owned by the state, a collective, or another person, that part of the will shall be deemed invalid.

39. If a testator's act during his or her lifetime is contrary to the intention expressed in the will, causing the property disposed of by the will to be lost, partially lost, or its ownership transferred or partially transferred before the commencement of inheritance, the will is deemed to be revoked or partially revoked.

40. If a citizen's testamentary letter contains provisions regarding the disposition of his or her personal property after death, and it truly represents the decedent's intent, is signed by the decedent, and bears the year, month, and day, and there is no evidence to the contrary, it may be treated as a holographic will.

41. A testator must have capacity for civil conduct when making a will. A will made by a person without capacity for civil conduct is invalid, even if such person later acquires capacity for civil conduct. If a testator had capacity for civil conduct when making a will but later loses such capacity, the validity of the will is not affected.

42. If a testator makes several wills in different forms with conflicting content, and there is a notarized will among them, the last notarized will shall prevail; if there is no notarized will, the last will made shall prevail.

43. If a testamentary succession or legacy is subject to a condition, and the condition can be fulfilled but the heir or legatee fails to fulfill it without justifiable reason, upon the request of the beneficiary or another heir, the people's court may cancel the right of such heir or legatee to receive the portion of the estate subject to the condition, and the heir or beneficiary making the request shall be responsible for fulfilling the condition in accordance with the testator's wishes and shall receive the estate.

IV. Handling of the Estate

44. When the people's court is adjudicating an inheritance case, if it is aware of an heir but is unable to notify such heir, when distributing the estate, it shall reserve the share of the estate that such heir should inherit and designate a custodian or custodian unit for that share.

45. If the share of the estate that should be reserved for a fetus is not reserved, it shall be deducted from the estate inherited by the heirs.

If the share of the estate reserved for a fetus, if the fetus is born alive but then dies, shall be inherited by its heirs; if the fetus is stillborn, the share shall be inherited by the decedent's heirs.

46. If an heir's renunciation of the right of inheritance causes him or her to be unable to perform a legal obligation, the act of renunciation is invalid.

47. An heir's renunciation of inheritance shall be communicated in writing to the other heirs. If the renunciation is made orally, and the heir admits it, or there is other sufficient evidence to prove it, it shall also be deemed valid.

48. During litigation, if an heir orally expresses renunciation of inheritance to the people's court, a written record shall be made and signed by the heir renouncing inheritance.

49. An heir's expression of intention to renounce inheritance shall be made after the commencement of inheritance and before the distribution of the estate. If the renunciation is expressed after the distribution of the estate, it is no longer a renunciation of the right of inheritance but of ownership.

50. If, before the estate is disposed of or during litigation, an heir repents the renunciation of inheritance, the people's court shall decide whether to recognize the repudiation based on the specific reasons put forward by the heir. If the repudiation occurs after the estate is disposed of, it shall not be recognized.

51. The effect of renunciation of inheritance shall be retroactive to the time of commencement of inheritance.

52. If, after the commencement of inheritance, an heir does not express renunciation of inheritance and dies before the distribution of the estate, the right to inherit the estate shall be transferred to his or her lawful heirs.

53. If, after the commencement of inheritance, a legatee expresses acceptance of the legacy and dies before the distribution of the estate, the right to accept the legacy shall be transferred to his or her heirs.

54. For the estates of martyrs whose living expenses are provided by the state or collective organizations, and of urban residents receiving social relief, the lawful heirs shall still be allowed to inherit.

55. When a collective organization provides "five guarantees" (food, clothing, medical care, housing, and burial expenses) to a "five-guarantee household," if there is a support agreement between the parties, it shall be handled according to the agreement; if there is no support agreement, and the decedent has a testamentary heir or statutory heir who requests inheritance, it shall be handled according to testamentary succession or statutory inheritance, but the collective organization has the right to request a deduction of the "five guarantees" expenses.

56. If a supporter or collective organization enters into a legacy-support agreement with a citizen, and the supporter or collective organization fails to perform its obligations without justifiable cause, leading to the termination of the agreement, such supporter or collective organization shall not enjoy the right to receive the legacy, and the support expenses paid shall generally not be compensated; if the legator fails to perform his or her obligations without justifiable cause, leading to the termination of the agreement, the legator shall reimburse the supporter or collective organization for the support expenses already paid.

57. When an estate with no heir is taken over by the state or a collective organization, if a person who may be given an appropriate share of the estate under Article 14 of the Inheritance Law makes a claim to obtain the estate, the people's court shall, depending on the circumstances, give an appropriate share.

58. When the people's court distributes houses, means of production, and property necessary for a specific occupation in the estate, it shall handle the matter in a manner conducive to the beneficial use of such property and taking into account the actual needs of the heirs and the interests of all heirs.

59. The people's court may, at its discretion, reduce the share of the estate to be inherited by an heir who intentionally conceals, misappropriates, or disputes the estate.

60. After the commencement of an inheritance action, if among the heirs or legatees there are those who are unwilling to participate in the action and do not express renunciation of substantive rights, they shall be added as co-plaintiffs; if they have clearly expressed renunciation of inheritance, they shall no longer be listed as parties.

61. If among the heirs there is a person who lacks the ability to work and has no source of income, even if the estate is insufficient to pay off debts, an appropriate share shall be reserved for such heir, and then the debts shall be paid off in accordance with Article 33 of the Inheritance Law and Article 180 of the Civil Procedure Law.

62. If the estate has been distributed but debts are not yet paid off, and there are both statutory and testamentary succession and legacies, first, the statutory heirs shall use the estate they have obtained to pay off the debts; if the debts cannot be fully paid, the remaining debts shall be paid by the testamentary heirs and legatees in proportion to the estate they have obtained; if there are only testamentary succession and legacies, the testamentary heirs and legatees shall pay the debts in proportion to the estate they have obtained.

V. Supplementary Provisions

63. For foreign-related inheritance, if the estate consists of movable property, the law of the decedent's domicile shall apply, that is, the law of the country of the decedent's last domicile before death.

64. For inheritance cases that have been finally adjudicated by the people's court before the implementation of the Inheritance Law, if a retrial is initiated through trial supervision procedures after the implementation of the Inheritance Law, the relevant policies and laws in effect at the time of the final judgment shall apply.

For inheritance cases that were accepted before the Inheritance Law took effect but had not been finally adjudicated at the time of its effectiveness, the people's court shall apply the Inheritance Law. However, the action may not be dismissed on the ground that the limitation period has expired.
